abstract: Maintains patient in-flight monitoring readiness and clinical pressure altitude constraint records
system_message:
You are the Aeromedical clinical director (MED). Your responsibilities include maintaining patient in-flight monitoring readiness and clinical pressure altitude constraint records, as well as overseeing blood product logistics for aeromedical evacuation corridors.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Blood product logistics（BLOOD）
information_points.content:
MED-BLOOD-7QU：For the Liard Basin High-Altitude Direct, mobile cooler inventory accounts for 4 units of packed red blood cells available for aeromedical transfer.
MED-BLOOD-OA1：For the Fort Simpson Ridge Transit, mobile cooler inventory accounts for 8 units of packed red blood cells available for aeromedical transfer.
MED-BLOOD-R5K：For the Nahanni Canyon Low-Level Vector, mobile cooler inventory accounts for 6 units of packed red blood cells available for aeromedical transfer.

information_points.title: Maintains patient in-flight monitoring readiness and clinical pressure altitude constraint records（ICU）
information_points.content:
MED-ICU-26U：For the Fort Simpson Ridge Transit, in-flight intensive care telemetry is active across the continuous patient monitoring datalink, and the maximum cabin pressure altitude reached during evacuation cruise is 2100 m.
MED-ICU-AWW：For the Nahanni Canyon Low-Level Vector, in-flight intensive care telemetry is active across the continuous patient monitoring datalink, and the maximum cabin pressure altitude sustained during evacuation cruise is 1500 m.
MED-ICU-7HM：For the Liard Basin High-Altitude Direct, in-flight intensive care telemetry is active across the continuous patient monitoring datalink, and the maximum cabin pressure altitude during evacuation cruise is 1800 m.
